cold_open.hook: Meta just jumped 10.32%—because apparently the solution to having too much AI compute is to become a cloud company.

markets.macro_note: Broad market flat; mega-cap tech diverging hard—Meta soars on cloud pivot while chip stocks crater on compute glut fears.

big_story.story_title: Meta, like SpaceX, looks to turn excess AI compute into cash
big_story.angle: Meta and SpaceX are both sitting on massive infrastructure they built for one thing and are now monetizing the overflow—the difference is SpaceX had a plan for it, Meta is improvising in real time.

quick_hits.angle: Getty-Shutterstock merger cleared in the US but killed by UK regulators—a reminder that antitrust theater is now geographically fragmented and unpredictable.
Warsh says the Fed will hint at rate moves only when they 'shut the door'—which is Fed-speak for 'we're not telling you anything until we've already decided.'
Venice AI hits unicorn status on a privacy-first pitch—in a market where every other startup is selling your data to train models, being boring about privacy is somehow the contrarian move.
England just had its warmest June on record—which is either climate news or a setup for why London tech conferences are now unbearable.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Rhythm Heaven never misses a beat—a Nintendo game so rhythmically precise it makes your own sense of timing feel broken.

sign_off.callback_target: Meta's cloud pivot—the overflow problem that became a business model
